The long-word splitting and the empty-input fix look right. But switching the line-fit check from `<=` to `<` contradicts the docstring ("lines of at most `width` characters"; append a word "if the resulting line is at most `width` characters long"). Only one test needs this change: `test_meeting_reminder`. "The meeting has been" is exactly 20 characters at width 20, the docstring says it fits, and the test expects it to wrap. Every other test passes with `<=` plus chunk splitting, so `<` was picked to make that one test pass. It also makes the behavior inconsistent: a single chunk can still fill the whole width ("https://ex" at width 10), but joined words can never reach it. The PR says this "matches the spec the notifications team agreed to," but nothing in the repo supports that, and the written spec says the opposite.

The test and the docstring conflict, so please raise it with the teammate instead of quietly changing the code. Either the test is right, in which case update the docstring and apply the exclusive rule consistently, including to chunk length. Or the docstring is right, in which case the test has an off-by-one and the notifications team needs to confirm the fix. Minor: the `if word:` guard is never needed, and the early `return []` and the `if current:` check do the same job.
